t:
(a) In General.—Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report setting forth the status of any efforts of the Secretary to determine whether to promulgate new regulations to add to the list of diseases for which a presumption of 
service-connection is warranted for purposes of section 1110 of title 38, United States Code, by reason of having positive association with exposure to an herbicide agent. 
    (b) Contents.—The report submitted under subsection (a) shall include the following:
        (1) A detailed explanation of any delays in making a determination described in such subsection. 
        (2) An estimate of the cost of adding to the list of diseases described in such subsection. 
        (3) The date the Secretary anticipates on which the Secretary will promulgate new regulations as described in such subsection.  
    (c) Definition of Herbicide Agent.—For purposes of this section, the term “herbicide agent” has the meaning given such term in section 1116 of title 38, United States Code.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to "consultation" and to promulgating "new regulations" signal participation. But the consultation is between two federal officials (the VA Secretary and the OMB Director), and the only duty imposed is a status report to congressional committees, all inside the federal government. The section neither requires nor authorizes rulemaking; it only asks for a report on whether and when the Secretary might issue regulations under existing authority.
fable.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report

opus.w: Every actor here is inside the federal government: the Secretary consults with the OMB Director and reports to congressional committees. The mention of regulations is tempting, but the section only asks for a status report on possible future rulemaking. It does not require or authorize any rulemaking, comment period, or outside consultation.
opus.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report setting forth the status of any efforts of the Secretary to determine whether to promulgate new regulations
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** The section mentions "promulgate new regulations," and rulemaking counts as participation, so this could look like a Yes. It also says "in consultation with," which sounds like participation.

**Why that reading fails:** The section doesn't require or authorize any rulemaking. It only requires a status report on whether the Secretary might issue regulations. The consultation is with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, who is a federal official. The report goes to congressional committees, which are also inside the federal government. No outside party takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to consult with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (a federal official) and submit a report to Congressional committees. Both the OMB Director and Congress are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes intra-government coordination and reports to Congress from the definition of participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the public, states, or non-federal experts in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget" constitutes participation because it involves coordination before a decision (submitting the report). However, the Director of OMB is a federal official inside the executive branch. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination between federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and is not participation. Furthermore, the report is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government.
